title: function-calling-parse-incident-breadcrumbs-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Small customer reported intermittent failures when using function/tool calling with structured JSON outputs. Failures surface as a 'parse error' in our function-caller wrapper (lib/structured_parser), not a model crash.
- Repro observed on prod-ish dataset (long chat history, >2k tokens).
- Working hypothesis: model sometimes emits trailing human text after a JSON object, or emits JSON-like but invalid values (single quotes, Python None, trailing commas, ellipsis).

Commands & experiments run so far:
1) Capture raw model stream via local debug harness:
   cmd: ./bin/redwood-func-call-run --model rwd-gpt-open-3 --history example_session.json --output raw_stream.txt
   Observed: stream contains a valid JSON object followed immediately by extra text after the closing brace.

2) Run lib/structured_parser against raw_stream.txt -> fails with JSONDecodeError: Expecting value at line 1 column 2045.
   Stack snippet: JSONDecodeError(\"Expecting value\", doc, 2045)

3) Tolerant parse fallback (regex trim trailing non-brace chars) -> json.loads succeeds for this trace, but other sessions still fail.

4) Reduce history length and re-run: parse failure rate drops significantly. Suggests context-length affects generation and sometimes triggers assistant commentary after structured output.

Error snippets observed (sanitized copies):
- "{\"status\": \"ok\", \"result\": {\"id\": 123, \"value\": \"X\"}}\nSure, I also think..."  # valid JSON followed by commentary
- "{'status': 'ok', 'result': None}\n"  # single quotes + Python None
- "{\"status\": \"ok\", \"items\": [1,2,],}"  # trailing comma
- Stream cut mid-object: "{\"status\": \"ok\", \"result\": {\"id\": 12" (EOF)

Quick hypotheses:
- Model sometimes appends follow-up commentary immediately after the JSON when uncertain.
- Long histories change tokenization/alignment near end-of-call, yielding partial objects or EOF mid-JSON.
- Model occasionally emits Python-isms (None, True/False, single quotes).
- Streaming reassembly bug: chunks delivered out-of-order or delimiters dropped, producing non-contiguous JSON fragments.

Planned next steps / TODOs:
- Add telemetry to capture raw top-k tokens around function call end for failing sessions (distinguish commentary vs streaming noise).
- Implement sanitizer heuristic chain in lib/structured_parser (order):
   a) strict json.loads -> on failure:
   b) trim trailing non-json junk after closing brace/bracket
   c) replace matched single-quote strings with double-quotes (conservative)
   d) convert Python None/True/False to null/true/false
   e) remove trailing commas in arrays/objects with a lightweight sanitizer
   f) if still failing, return original error and log full raw stream for analysis
  Log which heuristic succeeded (metric: parse_sanitize_success) and failures (parse_sanitize_failure).
- Expose strict_mode flag to customers (default tolerant=false -> tolerant parsing by default; strict_mode=true to error on any non-strict JSON).
- Investigate streamer reassembly: ensure frames are re-concatenated in order; add sequence ids to stream frames if not present.
- Create reproducible prompt that causes model to append commentary after JSON to test mitigations (explicit stop tokens and strong instruction: \"OUTPUT ONLY JSON OBJECT, NOTHING ELSE\").
- Run A/B test: reduced history window vs full history to quantify failure delta.

Questions for SRE/serving-runtime teams:
- Any recent changes to streaming chunk sizes, chunk-merging behavior, or frame boundaries (Jan 2026 deploys)?
- Any tokenization/compiler changes for open models that might affect end-of-output behavior?

Immediate SDK patch plan (developer-experience):
- Implement sanitizer chain behind feature flag in lib/structured_parser; add robust logging and metrics.
- Deploy to dev cluster; monitor parse_sanitize_success and parse_sanitize_failure.
- If sanitizer causes incorrect parsing of intentionally non-JSON outputs (data integrity risk), rollback via feature flag.

Validation plan / success criteria:
- If comment-followup root cause: traces will show '}' followed by alphabetical characters (e.g., \"Sure,\"). If streaming partials root cause: traces will show EOF inside JSON or evidence of out-of-order frame sequence ids.
- Run 1k synthetic long-history chats through SDK harness and compare parse failure rate before/after sanitizer.

Open/Unresolved:
- Default parity: Is tolerant parsing acceptable for platform default? For regulated customers we must offer strict parsing as opt-in.
- Model update risk: upstream model changes could alter failure patterns; pin models for Dedicated/Private or surface guidance to customers.

Rollback trigger:
- If sanitizer causes silent data corruption (parses non-JSON into JSON), disable feature flag and escalate.

Related tickets & links:
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/456 (draft sanitizer PR)
- JIRA DX-1284 (customer incident)
- JIRA DX-310, DX-987 (historical single-quote/None patterns)
- Confluence: DEVX-structured-output-guidelines

Notes / breadcrumbs:
- Capture raw_stream.txt for failing sessions and attach to ticket before any sanitizer is applied.
- Keep customer updated: explain we'll roll out tolerant parser behind flag and provide strict_mode option.

-- maya
